messages:

Subject: Ops playbook request: region lock + snapshot retention for audits

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Quick context: Medicore is finalizing our security acceptance criteria and we need concrete operational language from vendors around two things before legal signs off on DPA Exhibit C:

1) Region-locking / affinity: can you provide the exact operational playbook you follow when a customer requests region affinity (EU-only)? We need the runbook-level steps, responsible teams, and conditions for temporary cross-region processing.

2) Incident snapshots & retention: in certain incident scenarios we must be able to request a short-lived snapshot of activity (logs/traces and a data snapshot) for a forensic audit. We need to confirm: a) maximum snapshot availability window (we expect 72 hours max); b) where snapshots are stored and whether they may transiently leave the EU for processing; c) who has KMS access; and d) how you delete snapshots after the retention window.

Can you send a short playbook and indicate whether Redwood can commit to documented 72-hour snapshot retention, plus a subprocessor roster for any transient processing? We have an internal timeline — procurement wants this by EOD Wednesday so Legal can finish the redline.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lindstrom
DPO, Medicore Health

[Attachment: Medicore-context-summary.pdf (referenced)]

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lindstrom <sara.lindstrom@medicore.health>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, procurement@medicore.health

Subject: Re: Ops playbook request: region lock + snapshot retention for audits

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers up front: yes, we can provide a formal ops playbook and we can support a 72-hour snapshot retention window for forensic requests with defined controls, subject to the subprocessor roster and KMS constraints detailed below.

I've attached a draft playbook and a short checklist we use operationally. Summary of key points (short):
- Region affinity: customers may pin to a primary region (example: eu-west-1). We run an isolation policy that favors in-region compute and KV caches; background replication is disabled for pinned data except for controlled transient failovers.
- Transient failover: in capacity or DR incidents we may route to a compatible region (we call this a "transient hop"). Any transient hop is limited to a maximum of 48 hours by default but can be extended to 72 hours for approved forensic snapshots with customer consent and an audit record.
- Snapshots for forensics: we support on-demand snapshot creation (data + request-level telemetry). Snapshots can be created in-region; if specialized analysis requires controls not available in-region, an authenticated transient processing job may run in another Redwood region (we record this and notify the customer). Snapshots are encrypted with customer-isolated KMS keys when configured, and access is logged.
- Deletion: snapshots are scheduled for automated deletion after the agreed retention window; deletion runs are audited and a deletion receipt can be provided.

Open items we need from Medicore to commit in writing:
1) Whether you require customer-managed KMS (recommended for Exhibit C) or will accept Redwood-managed keys for dev/test artifacts.
2) Acceptance of transient processing only under explicit, documented approval (we will include an in-console approval flow + email notification).
3) Which subprocessor tolerance level you require (full roster + SOC2 evidence vs. named-exception only).

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa will coordinate a 30-min call with Medicore procurement/legal tomorrow to walk through the draft playbook.
- Kimberly, please confirm any DPA redline items we should pre-acknowledge (esp. KMS / subprocessor clauses).

Attachments: RDW-ops-playbook-region-lock-draft.pdf (playbook draft), quick-checklist.txt

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Sara / team — thanks for the clear asks. Legal review notes below; I'm attaching a redline of Exhibit C with suggested language. Highlights: 

1) 72-hour snapshot window: we can accept an enforceable 72-hour default retention for on-demand forensic snapshots created at customer request, provided the customer: (a) acknowledges potential transient processing for specialized analysis, and (b) agrees to the subprocessor roster we provide. If Medicore requires an absolute ban on any cross-border transient processing under any circumstance, we need to scope out alternative tooling (customer-managed analysis pipeline or on-prem deployment) — that would be a separate SOW.

2) KMS: we recommend customer-managed KMS keys for any snapshot artifacts containing PHI. If Medicore opts for Redwood-managed keys, we will ensure split-key controls and role separation; however, Exhibit C will require additional SOC evidence before final sign-off.

3) Subprocessors: we'll provide the full transient-processor roster plus SOC2 evidence. For items that are sensitive (third-party analytics used only for telemetry during snapshot processing), we can sign a named-exception clause that requires pre-approval for each use.

4) Audit receipts: we can provide automated deletion receipts and an audit trail in the Console. We'll add the deletion receipt wording to Exhibit C.

I'll attach the redline (Medicore-DPA-Exhibit-C-redline.pdf). If this looks good to you, Sean — please confirm the operational controls so we can produce the final combined doc for Medicore before the call.

Best,
